clue.text: Quickly replace the poster

indicators.note: to replace things is to put them back in a new place, so the letters of poster are set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to swap out a poster on the wall without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace' tells you to rearrange the letters of POSTER; 'the' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical tempo marking meaning very fast, so it is used to mean rapidly.

clue.text: Speech written on an envelope

definitions.meaning: a formal talk given to an audience
the street, town and postcode put on a letter

explanation.definitionFit: An address is both a formal oration and the postal location written on mail.

clue.text: Wound completely in a painful way

parts.note: to wound someone is to hurt them
fully means entirely

explanation.surface: Someone describes being injured thoroughly and agonisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurtfully is the adverb from hurtful, describing something done so as to cause pain.

clue.text: Run away with this French woollen coat

parts.note: to run away is to flee
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: Someone escapes wearing a French wool jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this French' asks for the French word for 'this', CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is the woolly coat of a sheep, and also a warm jacket.

clue.text: Is able to include a foot of a long garment

indicators.note: one word is told to take in other letters, so they sit within it

parts.note: is able means can

explanation.surface: A long robe is apparently able to accommodate an extra foot of length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is able' reads as part of the sentence but supplies the container; 'to include' says it takes the other two pieces in.
explanation.definitionFit: A caftan (also kaftan) is a loose ankle-length tunic from the Middle East.

clue.text: Force their majesties into trade

indicators.note: one piece is pushed into another, so it ends up surrounded by it

parts.note: to force someone is to coerce them
MM is the abbreviation for Their Majesties

explanation.surface: The king and queen are compelled to go into business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their majesties' uses the doubled abbreviation for a plural royal title; 'into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is buying and selling, the activity of business.

clue.text: Brilliant news item?

definitions.meaning: showy and dazzling, as in a smart, expensive look
a short urgent bulletin, a newsflash

explanation.definitionFit: Flash means ostentatiously smart in British slang, and a flash is a brief breaking-news report.

clue.text: Can align members of a church

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Can align members of a church (8)': ANGLICAN is an anagram of CAN ALIGN, but no clue word signals the anagram, so the indicator seems lost in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: Can align members of a church

clue.text: Quadruple one's efforts perhaps

parts.note: doubling something already doubled makes four times; one also speaks of making efforts twice as hard again

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to try four times as hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a doubled bid can be doubled again, multiplying the scores; and the stock phrase is to do this to one's efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: To redouble is to double again, which multiplies by four, and to intensify one's efforts.

clue.text: Feature about doctor who will proceed with the trade ban

indicators.note: one word goes round another, with the second inside it

parts.note: an ear is a feature of the face
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: A story about Doctor Who carrying on despite a ban on trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor who' looks like the TV show, but 'who will' is only linking; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official order prohibiting commerce with a country.

clue.text: Fish and meat eater

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme Jack who could eat no fat, only lean meat

explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small fish, and Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme ate only lean meat.

clue.text: Cloth found on desert animal

definitions.meaning: the coat growing on a dromedary or Bactrian

explanation.definitionFit: Fabric woven from the fibre of the desert beast's coat is named after it, and that coat literally covers the animal.

clue.text: A divine annex

parts.note: a divine is a theologian, and DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A clergyman joins something on to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex is to attach or append, as to put on extra.

clue.text: Old boy's better out of sight

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, with the possessive S
someone better after illness is cured

explanation.surface: A former pupil has recovered and disappeared from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscured means hidden or concealed from view.

clue.text: Tom, before a game of cards, has a sleep

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
nap is a card game, short for napoleon

explanation.surface: Tom, about to play cards, dozes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light doze, a brief rest.

clue.text: Might it be produced by an out-of-this-world baker?

definitions.text: Might it be produced by an out-of-this-world baker?

parts.words: Might it be produced by an out-of-this-world baker?
parts.note: a heavenly baker, one of the winged host, would bake something named after itself

explanation.surface: A question about what a superb baker might turn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a light sponge made with egg whites, named for its airy heavenly texture.

clue.text: One presumably does not mind being sold a pup?

definitions.text: One presumably does not mind being sold a pup?

parts.words: One presumably does not mind being sold a pup?
parts.note: being sold a pup means being cheated, but someone fond of hounds would be glad to buy a young one

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't care about being swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'sold a pup' is a British idiom for being conned with a worthless purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adores canines would welcome acquiring a puppy.

clue.text: Note found in the French meadow

parts.note: le is French for the
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: A note is discovered in a French field.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for grassland or pasture.

clue.text: Exorbitant demand from an old lawsuit

parts.note: ex means former
an action is a legal case

explanation.surface: An excessive claim arising from a former court case.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is the extortionate demanding of money or payment.

clue.text: Study in garden shed

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words garden shed, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Someone works in a garden shed as their office.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a small private room for work or relaxation.

clue.text: Officer and two hundred unknowns of little back-bone

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
C is 100 in Roman numerals, so CC is 200
x and y are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: An officer and a couple of hundred strangers lack backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: The coccyx is the small triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Mineral spring in southern US state

parts.note: PA is Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A mineral spring located somewhere in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a place with a natural spring of mineral water.

clue.text: Noel, upstanding, accepts prohibition in the country

indicators.note: one word takes in another, which goes within it
in a down clue, standing up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the name taken as written
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Upright Noel puts up with a ban somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upstanding' reads a word from the bottom up, giving LEON; 'accepts' means it takes the ban inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a nation on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Downtrodden place for an artist?

parts.note: a street artist draws in chalk on a walkway that is literally trodden down by passers-by

explanation.surface: An oppressed corner where a painter works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downtrodden' usually means oppressed but here is literal: walked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavement artist chalks pictures on the footway.

clue.text: An alto performed with no established key

indicators.note: music performed is worked through, so the letters of an alto are rearranged

explanation.surface: An alto sings a piece without a fixed key.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is composed without a tonal centre.

clue.text: The scholar left inside was a girl

indicators.note: one letter goes within the other pieces

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: The academic who left was a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Influential wealthy person will put novice in before actor breaks down

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second
one letter is put inside the word put

parts.note: L is a learner, a novice

indicators.note: something that breaks down falls apart, so actor is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rich person installs a beginner before the star collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' makes OCRAT, the anagram of the actor; 'in' places the learner within PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat holds power because of riches.

clue.text: Motor champion carries the lamp

indicators.note: the words Motor champion carry the letters within them

explanation.surface: A racing champion holds a light.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light; in Britain, a battery flashlight.

clue.text: Case of renegade in the establishment

indicators.note: one piece is put within the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the established church
a rat is a deserter or traitor

explanation.surface: An instance of a traitor within the ruling class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the establishment' means the Church of England (CE), England's state church.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden box for packing goods.

clue.text: Offer more and take the lot perhaps

definitions.meaning: to bid too high or outbid
bidding too much at auction may win the lot

explanation.definitionFit: To overbid is to offer above the value, which may secure an auction lot.

clue.text: Development area for the cameraman

parts.note: development here is of photographic film, done in a lightproof room

explanation.surface: A regeneration zone set aside for film crews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development area' suggests urban planning but means where film is developed.
explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom is an unlit room for processing photographs.

clue.text: Harp on about an unfortunate child

indicators.note: about here means around, in disorder, so harp on is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes on and on about a poor child.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphan is a child whose parents have died.
